question: Which of the following Vedas depicts the life of the early Vedic people of India and has a collection of 1028 hymns divided into 10 mandalas?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Rigveda__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest known Vedic Sanskrit text and is one of the four sacred canonical texts (śruti) of Hinduism known as the Vedas.
 
• It is composed of 1028 hymns (Suktas) divided into 10 books or mandalas.
 
• The hymns are dedicated to various deities, primarily the Rigvedic deities like Agni (Fire), Indra (the king of gods), and Soma (a sacred potion or plant).
 
• The Rigveda provides insights into the social, religious, and political life of the early Vedic people, making it a crucial source for understanding ancient Indian history and culture.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Samaveda
 Consists of melodies and chants, and is used primarily during the Soma sacrifice.
 
 

 2) Atharvaveda
 Contains hymns, spells, and incantations, focusing more on practical prayers for everyday life's prosperity, health, and healing.
 
 

 3) Yajurveda
 Comprises the liturgy (mantras) needed to perform the sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas, containing both prose and verse forms.
